name: Kraków
title: Kraków for New Year
lead: 28 December – 2 January, New Year in Kraków.

stay.label: Hotel
stay.name: Hotel Swing, Dobrego Pasterza 124, next to the Park Wodny water park, about 4.5 km north-east of the Main Square

facts: Out: Ryanair FR 8976, Mon 28 Dec, Sofia 11:40 → Kraków 12:20. Back: FR 8975, Sat 2 Jan, Kraków 07:00 → Sofia 09:50. Kraków is one hour behind Bulgaria.

Hotel Swing, Dobrego Pasterza 124, in Prądnik Czerwony, about 4.5 km north-east of the Main Square, next to the Park Wodny water park and the Krokus and Serenada shopping centres. Reception is open 24 hours. Breakfast is a paid extra; listings say a buffet from 07:00 to 10:00 for about 60 zł, so check when you book.
Sunrise around 7:35, sunset around 15:40. The best light is around 15:00.
Usually between −4 and 2 °C, often grey, with snow or sleet some days. Every outdoor stop has a plan B. Bring warm, waterproof shoes.

The hotel is out of the centre, so each day starts and ends with a ride. The new tram line to Mistrzejowice (open since 26 September 2026) runs along Dobrego Pasterza; the Park Wodny stop is outside the hotel. Tram 12 goes to Basztowa at the north edge of the Old Town (about 20 minutes) and on along Podwale and Piłsudskiego to Błonia and Salwator; tram 9 goes to Grzegórzki and Zabłocie, near Kazimierz and Podgórze; tram 16 goes to the main station (Dworzec Główny Tunel) and east to Nowa Huta. Buy tickets by card at the machine inside the tram; a 24-hour or 72-hour ticket is easiest. Plan every ride in the Jakdojade app, which also shows holiday timetables. Late at night, or for seven people with bags, use two Bolt or Uber cars: about 15 minutes to the Old Town.
Guides disagree on when the Main Square Christmas market ends: some say about 1 January 2027, others 26 December. Check krakow.pl before the trip.

Kraków bans fireworks from 2026, and the city does not run a fireworks show. Drinking alcohol in public is illegal and fined. Shops close early on 31 December and almost everything is closed on 1 January, so do the big shop on 30 December. Small Żabka shops are often open.
Polish złoty (PLN). Cards work almost everywhere; milk bars and small places can be cash only.
note: The maps are approximate, not to scale, and routes are straight lines between stops. Ridden legs (tram, taxi, plane) are dotted and not counted in the distance; the rows between stops say which tram to take and how long it takes. For the real street route use the “Open route” button. Opening hours, prices and dates come from public sources and may change; holiday hours around 31 December and 1 January especially. The “Photos” links open an image search.

days.title: Land, check in and a first evening
days.theme: The flight lands at 12:20. A ride across the city to the hotel, then straight into the Old Town for a late lunch, the Planty at dusk, the Christmas market, dinner and one drink.

stops.name: Land at Kraków Airport (KRK)
stops.d: Ryanair FR 8976 lands at 12:20, Kraków time (one hour behind Bulgaria). The hotel is on the other side of the city, about 20 km away. Easiest for seven people with bags: two Bolt or Uber cars straight to the hotel, about 30–40 minutes. Cheaper: the airport train to Kraków Główny (about 20 minutes; tickets at the machine on the platform), then tram 16 from the Dworzec Główny Tunel stop under the station to Park Wodny, about 15 minutes; about an hour door to door.
stops.q: Kraków Airport John Paul II Balice

stops.name: Check in at Hotel Swing
stops.d: Drop the bags; if the room is not ready yet, leave them at the 24-hour reception. Buy water and snacks at a Żabka or in the Krokus shopping centre next door.

go.by: Tram 12 from Park Wodny to Basztowa LOT
go.d: The Park Wodny stop is outside the hotel, by the water park. Tram 12 runs towards the centre through Rondo Mogilskie and Lubicz; get off on Basztowa street at the north edge of the Old Town. Buy tickets by card at the machine inside the tram.

stops.name: Late lunch at the Old Town's north edge
stops.d: All three are a few minutes from the Basztowa LOT stop.

opts.s: pierogi bar open around the clock, quick and cheap
all-day breakfasts, a modern take on the milk bar
candle-lit café tucked into a side street, with the Loch Camelot cabaret cellar below

stops.name: Planty park and the Collegium Maius courtyard
stops.d: Walk through the Planty, the green ring around the Old Town, to the Gothic courtyard of the oldest university building (Jagiellońska 15), just as the light goes (sunset around 15:40). The courtyard is free; if the gate is shut, look through it and carry on.

b.name: Bunkier Café, Plac Szczepański 3a
b.d: Skip the park and walk from Basztowa to Plac Szczepański, 5 minutes; warm up on the covered, heated terrace of Bunkier Café, then go on to the square.

stops.name: Christmas market on the Main Square
stops.d: Guides disagree on when the market ends: some say about 1 January, others 26 December, so check krakow.pl. Even without the stalls, the lit-up square is the place to start. Have a grzaniec (mulled wine) and try oscypek, smoked sheep's cheese with cranberry. Prices on the square are high, so have dinner elsewhere. On the hour, listen for the trumpet call (hejnał) from St Mary's tower.

stops.name: Dinner off the square
stops.d: Book a table for seven; December evenings fill up. An early dinner after the early flight.

opts.s: Polish dishes in a brick cellar, plus a cheap salad bar upstairs
highlander (góral) food at long wooden tables, good for groups, live folk music some nights
opts.q: Morskie Oko restauracja Plac Szczepański 8 Kraków

opts.s: cheap Polish home cooking, soup and pierogi, students' favourite

stops.name: One drink, then back to the hotel
stops.d: All three are a few minutes from the square.

opts.s: bar and small club with a hidden courtyard, DJs at weekends; 5 minutes from the square
craft beer bar in the Tytano complex, a former tobacco factory, 15 minutes' walk west of the square
legendary cabaret cellar under a palace on the square; check if there is a show
opts.q: Piwnica pod Baranami Rynek Główny 27 Kraków

go.by: Two Bolt or Uber cars to the hotel
go.d: From the Old Town, about 4–5 km. Before about 23:00 tram 12 from Basztowa LOT to Park Wodny also works, about 20 minutes.

stops.name: Back to the hotel
stops.d: Early night after the flight.

days.title: Wawel, Kazimierz and a sunset on Krakus Mound
days.theme: Tram 12 into town, a local market, the quiet streets up to Wawel Hill, lunch in Kazimierz, then over the footbridge to Podgórze for sunset from the oldest mound in the city. Dinner and bars in Kazimierz, a taxi back.

go.by: Tram 12 from Park Wodny to Basztowa LOT
go.d: The Park Wodny stop is outside the hotel, by the water park. Tram 12 runs towards the centre through Rondo Mogilskie and Lubicz; get off on Basztowa street at the north edge of the Old Town. Buy tickets by card at the machine inside the tram.

stops.name: Stary Kleparz market
stops.d: Locals' food market since the Middle Ages, open Monday to Saturday from early morning: fruit, pickles, cheese, sausage and pączki (Polish doughnuts). Partly covered. Buy an obwarzanek, the braided Kraków bagel, from one of the blue street carts on the way; about 3 zł. Two minutes from the Basztowa LOT stop.

stops.name: Breakfast in the Old Town
stops.d: Three places on the way south.

opts.s: candle-lit café tucked into a side street, with the Loch Camelot cabaret cellar below
all-day breakfasts, a modern take on the milk bar
old bohemian café, hot chocolate and cake

stops.name: Wawel Hill, then the river path to Skałka
stops.d: On the way, step into St Francis Basilica (free) for Stanisław Wyspiański's stained-glass window 'God the Father', then walk down Kanonicza, the quietest and oldest street in the Old Town, up to Wawel. The castle courtyards and the hill are free; the cathedral, state rooms and Dragon's Den are paid, and on 1 January many of them may be closed, so today is the day. Leave by the path down to the Vistula and walk along the river to Skałka, a Pauline church on a rock with a crypt where Polish poets and painters are buried. Few tourists get this far.

b.name: Wawel Cathedral
b.d: Spend the time indoors: the coronation cathedral, the royal tombs in the crypt and the climb to the Sigismund Bell. Paid; check hours on katedra-wawelska.pl.

stops.name: Zapiekanki on Plac Nowy (from the TikTok food guide)
stops.d: This is the place from the TikTok: the round market hall (Okrąglak) in the middle of Plac Nowy, ringed with zapiekanki windows. A zapiekanka is a long open baguette with mushrooms, cheese and toppings of your choice; a large one is cheap enough to share. Cash is safest; the queues move fast. The windows stay open late, so they work after the bars too.

opts.s: the best known window; open late, closed on Sundays according to In Your Pocket
another window in the same hall, the one TikTok creators feature most

opts.n: Cytat Café, Miodowa 23 (from the TikTok food guide)
opts.s: book café with quotes on the coffee cups and a wall of board games; for coffee after the zapiekanka

stops.name: Kazimierz courtyards and the Bernatek footbridge
stops.d: Walk Józefa and Szeroka streets and look into the courtyards. Then cross the Bernatek footbridge with its hanging acrobat sculptures to Podgórze.

stops.name: Sunset from Krakus Mound
stops.d: About 20 minutes uphill from the bridge. Free, open all the time, with a 360° view over the city; the sun sets around 15:40. Locals come here, tourists rarely do. The path gets muddy, so wear good shoes. On the way down, pass Ghetto Heroes Square with its 70 empty chairs.

b.name: MOCAK, Lipowa 4
b.d: Museum of Contemporary Art in the old Schindler factory complex, 15 minutes from the bridge. Check opening hours.

go.d: Down the hill, over the Bernatek footbridge and into Kazimierz. The hotel is too far to go back before dinner; warm up in a café on Józefa or Szeroka until 19:30.

stops.name: Dinner in Kazimierz
stops.d: Book for seven.

opts.s: Polish food and house-flavoured vodkas
small home-cooking place, big portions
bistro across the footbridge in Podgórze
opts.q: Zakładka Food and Wine Józefińska 2 Kraków

stops.name: Kazimierz bars
stops.d: Three of the classic Kazimierz bars, two minutes apart.

opts.s: candle-lit rooms, mismatched furniture, concerts in the cellar
huge bar in a former prayer house, with old murals on the walls
dark, candle-lit rooms and old furniture

stops.name: Late-night snack: the blue van sausage
stops.d: A Kraków ritual after the bars. From Plac Nowy it is 10 minutes' walk north to the market hall on Grzegórzecka; the van is cash only and closed on Sundays.

opts.s: grilled kiełbasa with mustard and bread from a blue 1970s van, from about 20:00 until 2–3 at night
opts.q: Kiełbaski z Niebieskiej Nyski Hala Targowa Kraków

opts.s: a second zapiekanka if you stayed in Kazimierz
pierogi round the clock, on the way home

go.by: Two Bolt or Uber cars to the hotel
go.d: From the market hall on Grzegórzecka, about 4 km. Tram 9 from the Hala Targowa / Grzegórzki area also runs to Park Wodny, but late at night a taxi is quicker.

days.title: Nowa Huta, the communist model town
days.theme: Nowa Huta is close to the hotel: a short tram ride east to the planned socialist-realist town of the 1950s, with a grand square, a milk bar unchanged since then and a church shaped like an ark. The big shop next to the hotel, a rest, then a club night in the Old Town.

stops.name: Breakfast at the hotel
stops.d: The buffet is a paid extra (see Good to know). Leave by 09:45.

go.by: Tram 16 east towards Pleszów, to Plac Centralny im. R. Reagana
go.d: From the Park Wodny stop the tram runs out through Mistrzejowice and Bieńczyce into Nowa Huta, much closer than from the centre. Check the exact stop in Jakdojade. Two Bolt cars take about 15 minutes.

stops.name: Plac Centralny and Aleja Róż
stops.d: The central square of the town planned in the 1950s, framed by grand socialist-realist blocks. Walk up Aleja Róż (Avenue of Roses), where a Lenin statue stood until 1989.

stops.name: Museum of Nowa Huta
stops.d: Branch of the Museum of Kraków in the former Światowid cinema (Osiedle Centrum E 1): life in the communist years. Check hours on mhk.pl. Guided tours of the Cold-War shelters under the town are run by private companies; book them a day ahead.
stops.q: Muzeum Nowej Huty Światowid Osiedle Centrum E 1 Kraków

stops.name: Arka Pana (Lord's Ark)
stops.d: Twenty minutes' walk north through the housing estates. A modernist church shaped like Noah's ark, finished in 1977 after a 20-year fight with the communist authorities. Free; be quiet during mass.

stops.name: Lunch on the square
stops.d: Back on Plac Centralny. Milk bars are cash only.

opts.n: Bar Mleczny Centralny, Osiedle Centrum C 1
opts.s: milk bar on the square since the early 1950s, soup and a main for very little
opts.q: Bar Mleczny Centralny Nowa Huta Kraków

opts.s: restaurant open since 1956, with the interior to match
Kraków's favourite ice cream, for dessert
opts.q: Good Lood Nowa Huta Aleja Róż Kraków

go.by: Tram 16 back towards the centre, to Park Wodny
go.d: The same line as this morning, the other way; check the stop in Jakdojade. Two Bolt cars take about 15 minutes.

stops.name: The big shop next to the hotel
stops.d: Shops close early on 31 December and nearly all are closed on 1 January, so buy food and drinks for New Year's Eve and New Year's Day now at a supermarket in the Krokus or Serenada shopping centre (Bora-Komorowskiego 37 and 41), a short walk from the hotel. Check their 30 December hours on Google Maps.

stops.name: Rest at the hotel
stops.d: Put the shopping away and rest; the sun sets around 15:40.

go.by: Tram 12 from Park Wodny to Basztowa LOT
go.d: Leave about 19:00. Tram 12 to Basztowa LOT, then 5–10 minutes on foot to dinner.

stops.name: Dinner in the Old Town
stops.d: Casual and filling before a night out.

opts.s: burgers, good for a group
Polish classics, duck and pierogi

opts.n: Czarna Kaczka, Poselska 22 (from the TikTok food guide)
opts.s: the duck place: roast duck with apples and sides, book for seven

stops.name: Club night
stops.d: Three Old Town clubs within 5 minutes of each other. Check the night's programme and entry fee on their pages.

opts.s: electronic club in a cellar labyrinth
bar and club, from indie to dance nights
big cellar club with two dance floors

go.by: Two Bolt or Uber cars to the hotel
go.d: Trams are rare after midnight; stay together and order both cars at once.

days.title: Salwator, Kościuszko Mound and New Year's Eve
days.theme: Tram 12 across town for a late brunch and a walk west along the river to the mound with the widest view of the city. A nap at the hotel, dinner, then the evening is blocked for New Year's Eve: pick one of three free options.

stops.name: Leave the hotel
stops.d: A late start.

go.by: Tram 12 towards Cichy Kącik, to the stop on Podwale nearest Felicjanek
go.d: Tram 12 runs through the centre along Basztowa, Dunajewskiego and Podwale; get off where Jakdojade shows the shortest walk to Felicjanek street, then a few minutes on foot.

stops.name: Brunch by the river
stops.d: Both Felicjanek cafés are two minutes from the Vistula.

opts.s: second-hand English bookshop with a café, cakes and quiches
quirky local café full of wardrobes and old furniture
roastery café with good breakfasts, on Krupnicza just west of the Old Town

stops.name: Salwator and the Norbertine convent
stops.d: Walk west along the Vistula to Salwator, an old village inside the city: the fortress-like Norbertine convent on the river and the little wooden church of St Margaret on the hill.

stops.name: Kościuszko Mound
stops.d: Uphill for 25 minutes along Aleja Waszyngtona. The mound stands inside a 19th-century fort; paid entry. On a clear day you can see the Tatra mountains.

b.name: National Museum, Al. 3 Maja 1
b.d: Polish 20th-century art and design, at the east end of Błonia; tram 12 runs past it on the way back. Hours on 31 December may be shorter; check mnk.pl.
b.q: Muzeum Narodowe Gmach Główny Al. 3 Maja 1 Kraków

stops.name: Back across Błonia
stops.d: The huge meadow where the Pope said mass; walk straight across it and through Jordan Park towards Krupnicza.

b.name: Tram 12 from Cichy Kącik
b.d: Skip the meadow: walk down to the Cichy Kącik loop and ride tram 12 back towards Podwale.

stops.name: Late lunch on the way back
stops.d: Shops close early today; you shopped yesterday.

opts.n: Pod Wawelem, Plac na Groblach 9 (from the TikTok food guide)
opts.s: huge schnitzels, ribs and beer by the litre in a loud beer hall, below Wawel
opts.q: Pod Wawelem Kompania Kuflowa Plac na Groblach 9 Kraków

opts.s: vegan Asian bowls and ramen, 5 minutes' walk
pierogi bar open around the clock, quick and cheap

go.d: From the Podwale or Basztowa stops. Holiday-eve timetables can be thinner; check Jakdojade.

stops.name: Nap and get ready
stops.d: Rest before a long night. Charge your phones and agree on a meeting point in case you lose each other at midnight (mobile networks get slow).

go.by: Tram 12 from Park Wodny to Basztowa LOT
go.d: Leave about 18:30. Tram 12 to Basztowa LOT, or two Bolt cars if you book a table further away.

stops.name: Dinner before the night
stops.d: Most restaurants serve set New Year's Eve menus that must be booked weeks ahead. If you cannot book, eat at the hotel restaurant or bring food from yesterday's shop and eat at the hotel before you go.

opts.s: highlander food, long tables for a group
opts.q: Morskie Oko restauracja Plac Szczepański 8 Kraków

opts.s: Polish dishes in a brick cellar
Polish classics

stops.name: New Year's Eve: pick one
stops.d: This time is blocked for New Year's Eve. All three are free to enter. Kraków bans fireworks from 2026 and the city no longer runs a show; the 2026/27 programme had not been announced in October 2026, so check krakow.pl and pik.krakow.pl in December. Drinking alcohol in public is illegal in Poland, and glass is usually not allowed on the square. From the hotel, the Main Square is the easiest to get back from; Krakus Mound is the furthest.

opts.s: the city's big open-air gathering in front of the Cloth Hall, traditionally free; recent years had a stage or light show and a countdown. the easiest to reach from the hotel: tram 12 to Basztowa LOT, then 5 minutes on foot

opts.n: Plac Nowy and the Kazimierz bars
opts.s: the square in Kazimierz fills up at midnight; bar-hop between Alchemia, Singer and Eszeweria, which usually have no entry fee, though some may sell New Year tickets, so check. 30 minutes' walk
the locals' alternative: watch midnight over the whole city from the top, quiet and free. Bring a torch and warm layers. 40 minutes' walk or 15 by taxi before 23:00

go.by: Back to the hotel: night tram, taxi or a long walk
go.time: about 55 min on foot from the Main Square
go.d: Taxis are scarce and expensive after midnight. From the Main Square it is about 4.5 km on foot, out along Lubicz to Rondo Mogilskie and up the tram line. Check in Jakdojade whether tram 12 or a night line runs that night; from Plac Nowy or Krakus Mound wait for a taxi or a tram rather than walk.

days.title: New Year's Day, slow
days.theme: A public holiday: most shops are closed and trams run less often. A late brunch, a walk along the river to the cliffs of the Zakrzówek quarry lake, an early dinner in Kazimierz and an early night, because the alarm rings at 04:00.

stops.name: Wake up slowly
stops.d: Leave at about 11:30.

go.by: Tram 12 from Park Wodny to Basztowa LOT
go.d: Trams run on a holiday timetable on 1 January, so check Jakdojade before you go out to the stop.

stops.name: Late brunch
stops.d: On 1 January opening hours are uncertain; check Google Maps before you go. Przypiecek is open round the clock.

opts.s: pierogi bar open around the clock, quick and cheap
all-day breakfasts, a modern take on the milk bar
French bakery with breakfast all morning

stops.name: Along the Vistula and over the Dębnicki bridge
stops.d: Walk down to the river and cross the Dębnicki bridge for the view back to Wawel from the other bank, then follow the streets of Dębniki south towards Zakrzówek.

b.name: Massolit Books & Café, Felicjanek 4
b.d: Sit out the rain with coffee and cake among second-hand books, two minutes from the bridge. Check that it is open on 1 January.

stops.name: Zakrzówek quarry lake
stops.d: Cross the Dębnicki bridge and walk 25 minutes south to the flooded limestone quarry: turquoise water under white cliffs, with paths along the top. The park is open in winter; the swimming pools are summer-only. Watch the sunset here around 15:45.

b.name: Kino Pod Baranami, Rynek Główny 27
b.d: Arthouse cinema in a palace on the square; films are shown in the original language with Polish subtitles. Check the 1 January programme.

stops.name: Ride to Kazimierz
stops.d: Two Bolt cars to Kazimierz, about 10 minutes, or a tram (Jakdojade). Warm up in a café until dinner; the hotel is too far to go back and forth.

stops.name: Last dinner
stops.d: In Kazimierz. Book ahead and check that they are open on 1 January.

opts.s: Israeli food, mezze for the table
French bistro, good value
tiny pierogi place with unusual fillings
opts.q: Pierogi MR Vincent Bożego Ciała 12 Kraków

stops.name: One last quiet drink
stops.d: Close to dinner, so you can be at the hotel by 22:00.

opts.s: bar with old Singer sewing machines as tables
cosy café-bar opposite Hevre
calm Old Town bar, on the way home

go.by: Two Bolt or Uber cars to the hotel
go.d: From Kazimierz, about 4–5 km. Before about 23:00 tram 12 from Basztowa LOT to Park Wodny also works, about 20 minutes. On 1 January trams are less frequent.

stops.name: Pack and sleep
stops.d: Book two taxis for 04:30 tomorrow (Bolt or Uber can schedule rides, or ask the 24-hour reception) and set alarms for 04:00.

days.title: Departure
days.theme: Flight FR 8975 leaves at 07:00 and lands in Sofia at 09:50 Bulgarian time.

stops.name: Wake up and check out
stops.d: Leave the key cards at the 24-hour reception.

stops.name: Two taxis to the airport
stops.d: From the hotel to Balice is about 20 km across the north of the city: about 25–30 minutes at night. Trams and the airport train do not help at this hour.

stops.name: Kraków Airport
stops.d: Check in online with Ryanair before you go. Security can be slow in the morning; the gate closes 30 minutes before departure.
stops.q: Kraków Airport John Paul II Balice

stops.name: Flight to Sofia
stops.d: FR 8975, Kraków 07:00 → Sofia 09:50 (Bulgarian time).
stops.q: Kraków Airport John Paul II Balice
